title: "A2 Simulation studies"
link-citations: true

Terminology: in silico study

## Definition and features
In simulation studies, researchers experimentally apply one or more methods to a large number of simulated datasets. Researchers generate these datasets under specified assumptions, usually with some element of randomness, so that the datasets mimic real studies. Software then systematically applies the method or methods to each dataset and measures outcomes such as precision or bias.

- A unique feature and strength is that one can modify the underlying truth, which allows assessing bias and the validity of precision measures under varying conditions.
- A limitation is that simulated scenarios may not fully capture the complexities of real studies with human error arising during data collection or methods application.

## Typical objectives and corresponding examples
[Propose a new method](../objectives/6propose-method.qmd): new alternative to the log-rank test.[@Magirr2026robust]

[Evaluate a single method](../objectives/7evaluate-method.qmd): random-effects meta-analysis;[@Hartung2001a] false positives when conducting subgroup analysis.[@Brookes2001subgroup]

[Compare methods](../objectives/8compare-methods.qmd): different methods for diagnostic meta-analyses with sparse data;[@Takwoingi2017performance] different methods for modeling multi-state disease progression;[@Huszti2011comparison] comparing two methods for correcting imperfect reference standards in diagnostic accuracy.[@UmemnekuChikere2021comparative]

[Develop guidance for understanding and applying methods](../objectives/9guidance-applying.qmd): guidance on using matching in cluster trials;[@Chondros2021when] guidance for variable screening in high dimensional survival analysis;[@Edelmann2020marginal] estimation of diagnostic test accuracy without reference standard.[@Sun2025estimation]
